newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Limited expansion approved at Maastricht airport.
newsitem.headline: Limited expansion approved at Maastricht airport.

text.p: The Dutch Cabinet has approved a limited expansion of the country's most southerly airport, a Ministry of Transport spokesman said.

Ton van Wijk, spokesman for the Dutch Transport Ministry, told Reuters in a telephone interview that the long running impasse over the expansion of Maastricht Aachen Airport between the Transport Minister Annemarie Jorritsma and the Environment Minister Margaretha De Boer was resolved during a cabinet meeting late Friday.

He said the airport is to be allowed two passenger charter aircraft to land every night. The airport's morning opening time for take-offs and landings will be extended by half-an-hour to 05.00 AM local every day.
In addition, the airport has won a green light for its proposed new 2,500 metres east-west runway.

Van Wijk commented: "It is not as much as the airport wanted, but you can see this is as a compromise between both ministers. The feeling is that Mrs Jorritsma is lucky to have secured two night time landings."

The charter aircraft will be restrcited to landing between the hours of 11: 00PM and 12:30PM lcoal, Van Wijk said. The agreement resolves a debate about expansion of the airport between the two ministries which had run for most of this year.

Cor Leverdingen, a spokesman for Maastricht Aachen Airport told Reuters the airport's management is disappointed that it will not be given permission for airfreight flights to land at night, part of its original proposal.

"It is not clear what the government's decision means for us, and we are waiting for a formal letter from the state which we hope will clarify the economic consequences for Maastricht Aachen Airport."

"From a cargo point of view, however, we've not been given much more than we already have. However, the new runway may have commercial implications for the airfreight sector. We have to sit down and study the decision, and draw our own conclusions," he added.

A joint working group of the airport's management and a team from Amsterdam's Schiphol airport are expected to study the Government's decision, and will give their opinion in the course of this month, he said.

The airport had hoped to persuade Dutch cargo and charter airline Martinair, 50 pct owned by KLM, to relocate some of its Schiphol airport-based airfreight activities to Maastricht. Leverdingen said the plan may now be more difficult to bring about, given the government's decision. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+44 171 542-5017
